q1_issues.issue: "Schwarzenegger's decision" is a genitive naming an event noun's underlying subject, which takes that noun's subject role (`Agent`/`Experiencer`); `Possession` there asserts a relation the text does not state (the "the committee's ruling" case).
`(Past sk_await_1)` tenses the participial reduced relative "those awaiting …", which carries no tense of its own — the matrix "was" holds the tense.

`await` is a distributive predicate over the definite group, so the per-member `(Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) …)` rule should accompany the group event — and a member (Riordan) is in fact named in the same sentence, which is exactly what the rule is for.

q2_gaps: privative / temporal adjective on a role noun ("former" mayor, "ex-") — nothing distinguishes it from an ordinary attributive, and the Past wrapper here only coincidentally covers it

a place name inside an occupational premodifier ("Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan") — the title phrase is routed "through Compound concepts", which explicitly excludes proper nouns, so the office-to-place link is unspecified
notes: The reduced relative, the `person` group witness (justified by discourse evidence, not the pronoun alone), the multi-word name symbols and the `Past`-wrapped appositive typing and `PartOf` are all handled correctly. `(Past (Possession richard_riordan los_angeles))` is a strained but defensible transposition of the premodifier rule onto a title realized as the person's own typing.
